column2: 中古英语 writing ← 古英语 wrīting，即 write ＋ 动名词后缀 -ing；write 一支 ← 原始日耳曼语 *wrītaną（刻、划）
column3: the activity of putting words on paper, or words so put
column5: Her writing has improved this term.|The writing on the label had faded.
column6: the putting down of words, and what is put down – 把话落成字这件事，以及落下的那些字
column7: 写作：把文字写出来这项活动|文字：写下来的那些字迹或篇章

column2: 中古英语 wrong ← 古英语 wrang（弯的、歪的）← 古诺尔斯语 rangr（歪、错）← 原始日耳曼语 *wrangaz（拧歪的）← 原始印欧语 *wer-（转、弯）；与 wring 同支
column3: not correct, or not in accordance with what is right
column5: You have the wrong number.|It was wrong of him to say that.
column6: bent away from what is correct – 从正确的那条上歪开了
column7: 错误的：与事实或标准不符|不对的：做法上不该如此

column2: 中古英语 yerd ← 古英语 ġeard（围地、园）← 原始日耳曼语 *gardaz（围起来的地）← 原始印欧语 *gʰerdʰ-（围）；「码」是另一支，← 古英语 gierd（杆、量尺）
column3: an enclosed area beside a building, or a unit of length
column5: The children play in the back yard.|The cloth is sold by the yard.
column6: a piece of ground fenced off beside a building – 房子旁边圈起来的一块地
column7: 院子：屋旁围起来的那块空地|码：长度单位，原以一根量杆为准，是同形异源的另一支

column2: 中古英语 yanen ← 古英语 ġinian（张口）← 原始日耳曼语 *ginōną；并与另一支 gānian 合流 ← 原始印欧语 *ǵʰeyh₁-（张口）
column3: to open the mouth wide and breathe in, from tiredness
column5: He yawned and rubbed his eyes.|She stifled a yawn during the talk.
column6: opening the mouth wide to draw a long breath when tired – 累了便张大嘴长吸一口气

column2: 中古英语 yeer ← 古英语 ġēar ← 原始日耳曼语 *jērą ← 原始印欧语 *yóh₁r̥（年、春）
column3: the period of twelve months, or the time the earth takes to circle the sun
column5: She has lived here for ten years.|Sales rose in the second year.
column6: the full round the earth makes about the sun – 地球绕日走完的那一整圈
column7: 年：十二个月的那段时间|年度：作为统计或行政单位的那一年

column2: 中古英语 yeerly ← 古英语 ġēarlīċ，即 year ＋ 形容词或副词后缀 -ly
column3: happening once every year
column5: They hold a yearly inspection.|The rent is reviewed yearly.
column6: coming round once in each turn of the year – 每一年里出现一次

column2: 中古英语 ȝellen ← 古英语 ġiellan（大叫）← 原始日耳曼语 *gellaną ← 原始印欧语 *gʰel-（喊、鸣）
column3: to shout loudly, often in anger or excitement
column5: He yelled across the pitch to her.|A yell came from the far room.
column6: letting the voice out at full force – 把声音全放出来
column7: 叫喊：高声喊出|喊叫：同义，偏重连续地喊

column2: 中古英语 yelow ← 古英语 ġeolu ← 原始日耳曼语 *gelwaz ← 原始印欧语 *ǵʰelh₃-（绿、黄）
column3: of the colour of butter or ripe lemons
column5: She painted the door bright yellow.|Yellow leaves covered the lane.
column6: the colour that lies between green and orange – 介于绿与橙之间的那种颜色
column7: 黄色的：形容颜色如柠檬如蜂蜜|黄色：那种颜色本身

column2: 中古英语 yes ← 古英语 ġīese（正是、当然），与 yea 同根
column3: used to give a positive answer
column5: Yes, that is exactly right.|He gave a firm yes to the offer.
column6: the word that grants what was asked – 用来应下所问的那个词
column7: 是：肯定对方所说|同意：把这份肯定用在意见或请求上

column2: 中古英语 yesterday ← 古英语 ġiestrandæġ，即 yester（昨）＋ day（日）
column3: on the day before today
column5: We met her only yesterday.|Yesterday was colder than today.
column6: the day that came just before this one – 紧在这一天之前的那一天

column2: 中古英语 yielden（付、交）← 古英语 ġieldan（偿付）← 原始日耳曼语 *geldaną（付）← 原始印欧语 *gʰeldʰ-（付）
column3: to produce something, or to stop resisting
column5: The field yields two crops a year.|He refused to yield to pressure.
column6: handing over what one has been holding – 把手里守着的交出去
column7: 产生：出产出成果，如同交出所得|屈服：不再抵抗，把立场交出去|产量：交出来的那个数量

column2: 中古英语 yong ← 古英语 ġeong ← 原始日耳曼语 *jungaz ← 原始印欧语 *h₂yuh₁en-（年少）
column3: having lived only a short time
column5: She looked young for her age.|The young of the species stay hidden.
column6: early in the span of a life – 处在一生里靠前的那一段
column7: 年轻的：人的岁数不大|幼小的：动植物还未长成

column2: 由 young ＋ 后缀 -ster 构成，17 世纪初始见；young 一支 ← 古英语 ġeong ← 原始日耳曼语 *jungaz
column3: a child or young person
column5: The youngsters ran ahead down the path.|He coaches youngsters at the club.
column6: one still in the early part of life – 还处在人生前段的那个人
column7: 年轻人：岁数轻的那些人|小孩：其中更小的那些

column2: 中古英语 youres，14 世纪起见于记载，即 your ＋ -s，仿 his 的构式而成；取代了标准语中的 yourn
column3: the one or ones belonging to you
column5: This coat is yours, not mine.|Our seats are here; yours are behind.
column6: the thing that belongs to the person addressed – 属于所说话对象的那一份
column7: 你的：归你所有之物|你们的：归你们几人所有之物

column2: 中古英语 yourself，即 your ＋ -self；self 一支 ← 古英语 self（自身）← 原始日耳曼语 *selbaz
column3: used to refer back to the person being addressed
column5: Did you cut your hair yourself?|Help yourself to more bread.
column6: pointing back at the person just addressed – 回指刚被称呼的那个人

column2: 中古英语 youthe ← 古英语 ġeoguþ（年少之时）← 原始日耳曼语 *jugunþō，即 young ＋ 抽象名词后缀 -th
column3: the period of being young, or young people as a group
column5: He spent his youth at sea.|The scheme is aimed at local youth.
column6: the early stretch of a life, and those in it – 一生里靠前的那一段，以及处在其中的人
column7: 青年：处在这个阶段的人|青春：这段时期本身

column2: 中古英语 zele ← 古法语 zel ← 晚期拉丁语 zelus ← 希腊语 zelos（热忱、妒意）← 原始印欧语 *yeh₂-（追求）；与 jealous 同源
column3: great energy in pursuit of a cause
column5: She threw herself into the work with zeal.|His reforming zeal never faded.
column6: energy poured into a cause one believes in – 为自己认定的事一股劲使出去
column7: 热情：对某事怀着强烈的心力|热忱：同义，偏书面，多用于正式场合

column2: 1600 年前后借自意大利语 zebra ← 葡萄牙语 zebra ← 古葡萄牙语 azebra（野驴）← 通俗拉丁语 *eciferus ← 拉丁语 equiferus（野马），由 equus（马）＋ ferus（野的）构成
column3: an African animal like a horse, with black and white stripes
column5: A herd of zebra crossed the plain.|No two zebras share the same pattern.
column6: a horse-like animal marked all over with black and white bands – 形似马、通体黑白相间成条带的兽

column2: 1712 年始见，借自法语 zigzag（1662 年始见），或出自日耳曼来源经瓦隆语 ziczac 传入；也可能取自字母 Z 的形状
column3: a line or course that turns sharply left and right in turn
column5: The path climbs in a zigzag up the slope.|He drew a zigzag across the page.
column6: a course that turns sharply back the other way again and again – 一路反复朝相反方向急折
column7: 之字形：这种左右折返的形状|曲折的：形容路线或过程这样折来折去

column2: 借自德语 Zink ← 中古高地德语 zinke（尖、齿）← 原始日耳曼语 *tindaz（尖齿）← 原始印欧语 *h₃dónts（牙、突出物）；因炼出时结成齿状晶而得名
column3: a bluish-white metal used to coat iron against rust
column5: The roof is coated with zinc.|Zinc protects the steel from rust.
column6: a bluish-white metal laid over iron to keep rust off – 覆在铁面上防锈的那种青白色金属

column2: 英语 zip 为拟声词，学那一声轻快的响
column3: to fasten with a zip, or to move very fast
column5: He zipped up his jacket and left.|A car zipped past the junction.
column6: a quick movement that closes or passes in one stroke – 一下就合上或掠过的那种快动作
column7: 拉上拉链：滑块一推把两排齿合到一起|快速移动：动作快到只留一声响

column2: 源自拉丁语 zona（腰带）← 希腊语 zone（束带、腰带），因地带在地图上呈条带状而得名
column3: an area marked off from those around it by some feature
column5: Parking is banned in this zone.|The council zoned the land for housing.
column6: a stretch marked off from its surroundings by one shared feature – 因某个共同特征而被从周围划出来的一片
column7: 区域：划出来的那一片地方|分区：把整片按用途划成几块这个动作

column2: 截自 zoological garden（动物学园）；zoological 一支 ← 希腊语 zoion（动物）＋ logia（学）
column3: a place where wild animals are kept for people to see
column5: The zoo opens at nine each day.|They took the children to the zoo.
column6: a place where wild animals are kept so people can see them – 圈养野生动物供人观看的地方

column2: 英语 zoom 为拟声词，1892 年前后始见，学那一声疾驰的呼响；镜头义 1930 年代由 zoom lens 而来
column3: to move very fast, or to change a camera's focal length
column5: Motorbikes zoomed along the seafront.|Zoom in on the top left corner.
column6: moving fast enough to leave only a rushing sound – 快到只剩一声呼响
column7: 迅速移动：极快地驶过或掠过|变焦：把镜头焦距迅速拉近或推远
